notes: §1985:XI.4.3.2 prints 'RETURN file-name-1 RECORD [ INTO identifier-1 ] AT END imperative-statement-1 [ NOT AT END imperative-statement-2 ] [ END-RETURN ]': AT END unbracketed (mandatory), NOT AT END only after it, RECORD an optional word. CobolIO.g4#returnStatement parses the shape, SortBinder#BindReturn refuses a missing AT END by role (COBOL1850, also when only NOT AT END is written), and VersionConformancePass#VisitConditionalPhrases (ConditionalPhrases#OutOfPrintedOrder) refuses NOT AT END before AT END at 85 as the 2002 relaxation (COBOL0900). Probes at --std 85: reversed order -> COBOL0900; NOT-only and bare RETURN -> COBOL1850; AT END written twice -> COBOL2269; 'RETURN f END ...' and 'RECORD AT END ... NOT END' run (A C DONE); RETURN INTO from an ODO SD record prints [A1Q     ] [C3XYZ   ] (current length, space-filled). The witness runs AT END/NOT AT END/END-RETURN in printed order and prints A B C DONE.

next.reason: 1985: "AT END imperative-statement-1 [ NOT AT END imperative-statement-2 ]"; 2023: "The AT END phrase and the NOT AT END phrase, when specified, may be written in reversed order.". The format is identical, but a 2023 syntax rule lets NOT AT END precede AT END. The 1985 format fixes AT END first, so 2023 accepts programs that 1985 refuses.
